records.title: RATuner: Retrieval-Augmented VLSI Flow Design Parameter Tuning Framework.
records.abstract: Optimizing configurable parameters in the Very-large-scale Integration (VLSI) design space is a key process for achieving high Quality-of-Result (QoR) metrics, including performance, power, and area. However, this task is severely challenged by the enormous design space, the lack of analytical mapping functions with QoR, and the high computational cost of evaluating each design choice. While Bayesian Optimization (BO) offers a balanced trade-off between exploitation and exploration, standard BO methods typically do not incorporate domain knowledge specific to VLSI design flow parameters. To address these limitations, we propose RATuner, a retrieval-augmented framework for high-dimensional VLSI Flow Design Space Exploration (DSE). RATuner integrates domain knowledge through a document-retrieval-based embedding method to guide Bayesian optimization, using design parameter embeddings constructed from EDA documentation. It further employs a stage-wise causal attention mechanism to model both intra-stage parameter interactions and the critical inter-stage causal dependencies present in the sequential VLSI design flow. Finally, an iterative Bayesian optimization strategy is utilized to achieve an efficient trade-off between exploitation and exploration. Experimental results on RISC-V and Blackparrot benchmarks show that RATuner achieves up to 33% improvement in Pareto-driven QoR metrics compared to representative state-of-the-art VLSI Flow DSE methods. The proposed framework bridges the gap between black-box optimization and VLSI domain expertise by incorporating domain knowledge, thereby improving the efficiency and quality of automatic VLSI design closure.

records.title: A quasi-experimental analysis of capabilities and limitations of generative AI in academic content evaluation in social sciences
records.abstract: The complexity of social sciences research and the limitations of traditional evaluation methods highlight the need to explore the capabilities and application potential of generative AI in academic evaluation. Previous research in fields such as biomedical and other natural sciences has demonstrated the potential of generative AI to estimate the quality of research articles. This study adopts a quasi-experimental approach, 100 volunteers produced 600 social sciences academic texts across 6 types of topics, which were evaluated by 8 mainstream generative AI models. Statistical and sentiment analysis was conducted to compare the evaluation results using zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies. The results show that AI-generated total scores are unreliable (precision = 66.35 %), and the actual total scores differ moderately from the human benchmark (average Cohen's d = 0.425). Few-shot prompt exhibited weaker differentiation capabilities across dimensions (average correlation = 5.25), while zero-shot prompt performed better (e.g., correlationClarity, Significance = 0.13), particularly in writing quality (average standard deviation = 5.38). Significant score differences were observed across the eight models (all p < 0.001), indicating inconsistency among models. Additionally, AI-generated comments across dimensions were generally positive, with different models exhibiting strengths across various dimensions and tasks. This study provides empirical evidence for scholars, peer reviewers, and research evaluation professionals interested in integrating generative AI into social sciences’ evaluation workflows. Overall, generative AI shows potential for enhancing evaluation efficiency and reducing favoritism in the peer review of social sciences, especially in large-scale or preliminary evaluations. However, when evaluating the novelty and significance, its dependency on domain knowledge and the interpretability of the results still requires prudent consideration and refinement.

records.title: MAF-GNN: Graph neural network-based multi-atlas brain functional information fusion for major depressive disorder diagnosis with rs-fMRI
records.abstract: Early diagnosis and analysis of major depressive disorder (MDD) are essential in the mental health field, with resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) frequently used to investigate disease-related abnormalities. Existing fMRI-based MDD studies present limitations, including neglecting the multi-scale nature of brain functional information and lacking clinical interpretability. To address these limitations, we propose a graph neural network-based multi-atlas fusion method (MAF-GNN) that integrates multi-scale brain functional information from complementary and selective perspectives through multi-head cross-attention fusion and adaptive atlas-weighted learning strategies. The synergistic integration of these two modules uniquely enables inter-atlas feature alignment and adaptive reliability weighting, achieving robust multi-atlas fusion and providing a comprehensive characterization of brain functional connectivity. Furthermore, we identify MDD biomarkers across three dimensions: abnormal brain regions, functional connectivity, and brain networks, revealing its neuropathological mechanisms and enhancing the model’s interpretability. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MAF-GNN in MDD (N=1570) and recurrent MDD (N=615) diagnosis tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods by an average accuracy margin of 2.8 % and 4.1 %, respectively. Moreover, the generalization experiment results on autism spectrum disorder (ASD) underscore its potential applicability to other psychiatric disorders. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZHChen-294/MAF-GNN.

records.title: API-DONet: A knowledge-guided deep neural operator network for flood forecasting
records.abstract: Deep operator networks (DeepONets), capable of learning mappings between input and output function spaces via the operator approximation principle, have become a widely used method in Earth sciences applications. However, when applied to flood time series forecasting, DeepONets struggle to model the complex dynamic evolution of spatiotemporal features and lack explicit incorporation of physical principles, limiting physical consistency and predictive accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose an adaptive physics-informed DeepONet (API-DONet), a knowledge-guided neural operator network for accurate and adaptive flood forecasting. Specifically, we introduce a newly designed U-CBAM module as the branch net to encode the spatiotemporal relationships between different channels. Additionally, a decoder guided by the enhanced Fourier neural operator is used to extract global features, facilitating rapid and effective flood prediction under nonlinear dynamic conditions. Importantly, we design the loss function of the proposed model based on flood physics theory, ensuring that the predicted results are more consistent with the principles of flood physics. Moreover, we extend an adaptive gradient descent-based adversarial training strategy that dynamically balances the trade-off between prediction accuracy and physical consistency. Experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that API-DONet outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy and consistency. Compared to benchmark models, RMSE and MAPE were reduced by 45.071% and 5.523%, respectively, while NSE and KGE increased by 5.182% and 22.058%, respectively. Code is available at https://github.com/KingslyZ/APIDNO.

records.title: From graphs to tokens: Substructure-aware molecular representation for large language models
records.abstract: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to process graph-structured data holds significant potential for advancing molecular research, especially in tasks related to molecular structure analysis and understanding. However, a key challenge remains in effectively tokenizing molecular graphs to align with the capabilities of LLMs. To bridge the gap, this paper proposes SubStructure-aware Tokenization (S2Token) that fragments molecules into chemically meaningful, reusable substructures. The key idea is to generate semantically enriched substructure token embeddings and represent the complex relationships between tokens in the LLM embedding space, allowing LLMs to learn and generalize chemical patterns effectively. To achieve this, S2Token begins by decomposing molecular graphs based on frequency and functionality to build a vocabulary. Then, we establish a dual-view token embedding method that jointly encodes fine-grained structural and functional attributes of molecular substructures. Furthermore, we propose an efficient token alignment strategy to associate the dependencies between non-sequential substructures with the LLM token embedding space. In this way, our method activates the LLMs’ generalization ability to unseen molecular graphs. To evaluate this, we curate four task-specific molecular datasets designed to investigate generalization. Extensive experiments on three standard benchmarks and four curated datasets demonstrate that S2Token consistently yields substantial performance improvements. On the molecular caption benchmark, S2Token achieves a 12.6% average performance gain across six metrics, outperforming the best LLM-based method. For forward reaction and retrosynthesis tasks, it enhances fingerprint similarity for synthesized molecules by 6.6% and 8.6%, respectively. Moreover, S2Token shows advantages on four generalist evaluation tasks, including 9.7% and 3.0% reductions in MAE on the molecular property prediction task, compared to graph- and node-centric tokenization methods. Code is available at https://github.com/GraphMoLab/S2Token.

records.title: Latent diffusion-augmented cross-modal representation learning for radiology report generation
records.abstract: Radiology report generation aims to produce comprehensive textual descriptions from medical images, enhancing diagnostic efficiency and alleviating the workload of radiologists. However, it often suffers from weak semantic expression of subtle lesions and inherent heterogeneity between visual and textual modalities. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Latent Diffusion-augmented Cross-modal Representation learning (LDCR), which enhances pathological representations and promotes deep cross-modal alignment. Specifically, LDCR introduces a Latent Diffusion Enhancement Module (LDEM) that simulates progressive degradation and semantic reconstruction in latent space through a diffusion mechanism, improving sensitivity to subtle pathological lesions. Building on latent diffusion-enhanced visual representation, a Heterogeneous Information Fusion Module (HIFM) is devised to bridge the modality gap by aligning visual and textual features in a shared semantic space Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks, IU X-ray and MIMIC-CXR, demonstrate that LDCR outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving improvements of up to 1.5%, 0.8% and 3.5% in BLEU-4, METEOR and ROUGE-L on IU X-ray, and 3.7%, 1.9% and 1.7% on MIMIC-CXR, respectively. The code is available at https://github.com/Eleanorhxd/LDCR.git.

records.title: MedCTM: A CNN-Transformer-Mamba Hybrid Network for Medical Image Classification
records.abstract: Medical image classification requires models that jointly capture local textures and long-range dependencies, while remaining efficient enough for practical use. To meet these requirements, we propose MedCTM, a CNN-Transformer-Mamba hybrid network. It decomposes feature learning into three complementary branches: local feature extraction, long-range dependency modeling, and cross-branch interaction. The core of MedCTM is the Bidirectional Channel Interaction Attention (BCIA) module. This module enables dynamic information exchange between CNN and Mamba features by allowing each to condition the other. A three-stage cascade is then used to progressively refine multi-scale representations. We evaluate MedCTM on eight medical image datasets that span seven modalities and over 100,000 samples. The model achieves strong performance with only 1.42-2.63 GFLOPs. On the average F1 score across the eight datasets, MedCTM outperforms the state-of-the-art MedViTv2 by 0.5%–1.7%, while using 12.9%–24.4% fewer parameters.

records.title: SocLitGen: An LLM-assisted framework for automated literature review in social sciences
records.abstract: Existing automated literature review technologies primarily target computer science contexts and face significant adaptability challenges in social science disciplines. Addressing this gap, this study proposes SocLitGen, a seven-module framework specifically designed for social science literature review generation. SocLitGen was evaluated using review tasks from management and economics topics on a corpus of 1,559,141 papers, comparing against Naive RAG, AutoSurvey, and graduate student writing. Baseline comparisons show that in citation quality (recall and precision), SocLitGen outperforms Naive RAG by at least 39.9%; in content quality (academic professionalism, structural rationality, and language fluency), SocLitGen outperforms AutoSurvey by at least 13.1% and graduate student writing by at least 9.5%. Cross-context evaluations reveal differentiated performance patterns: cross-disciplinary analysis confirms consistent performance across management and economics; cross-model experiments show Qwen2.5 performs optimally in academic and structural dimensions while GLM-4 excels in language fluency; cross-literature scale analysis demonstrates that large-scale sets enhance professionalism and structure but reduce fluency.

records.title: Hybrid machine learning solutions for mitigating climate-induced productivity losses in sustainable construction management
records.abstract: Climate change has contributed to increased weather extremes, which require new and proactive planning and workforce management practices in construction. This research created a hybrid machine learning model (HMLM) using XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost to predict construction worker productivity across a variety of weather conditions. We trained these models for a decade-long dataset capturing daily weather parameters and productivity in U.S. construction sites. The ensemble methods were able to reduce the root mean square error (RMSE) to 4.50, a 10 % improvement over the best single model. Using the RCP 8.5 scenario, our analysis predicts substantial effects upon construction productivity due to climate change. The SHAP analysis showed that precipitation and temperature together contributed 15 % of the model’s total mean absolute SHAP importance on the test set, indicating their strong model-based influence on predicted productivity (not causation). On top of this, our findings showcase that temperature fluctuations from 15 °C to 35 °C and humidity from 40 % to 70 % could impact productivity by 7.5 %, while productivity under ideal conditions could be at 92.5 %. Accordingly, the understanding of these events used in project management has shown reductions in delays of up to 30 days while in adverse situations. A strong implementation of such a concept is found in this research showing how a construction firm could improve workforce performance and project duration by adapting for climate, and producing data-informed decision making by as much as 25 % -this research strongly advocates for a proactive management process around climate variability and uncertainty.

records.title: Towards cleaner production of methyl glycolate: Techno-economic-environmental optimization via hybrid physics-machine learning modeling
records.abstract: The transition to sustainable chemical manufacturing requires a balance among technical feasibility, economic viability, and environmental impact. This challenge is particularly evident in the dimethyl oxalate to methyl glycolate (DTMG) process, a promising route for producing a key monomer of biodegradable polymers. To address these, this study develops a hybrid physics-machine learning framework for multi-objective optimization (HyMeO) of the DTMG process. It seamlessly integrates the strengths of process simulation, automated machine learning, and natural heuristic algorithms. A high-fidelity dataset of 1058 operational scenarios is generated via rigorous process simulation. Eight machine learning models are developed and automatically optimized, with the deep neural network model demonstrating the best performance (R2 > 0.96). The Shapley additive explains and partial dependency analyses are conducted to unveil the internal prediction mechanism of this model, which reveal that the distillate-to-feed ratio of the MG refining column and the hydrogen flowrate are the most influential factors governing the trade-offs between economic and environmental objectives. The preferred model coupled with the genetic algorithm to maximize exergy efficiency while minimizing production cost and CO2 emission of the DTMG process. The optimal solution achieves an 8.82 % increase in exergy efficiency, an 8.91 % cost reduction, and a 0.31 % decrease in CO2 emissions. Therefore, the proposed HyMeO framework can effectively reconcile the trade-offs among economic, technical, and environmental objectives in the DTMG process, providing a generalizable methodology for the sustainable intensification of chemical processes.

records.title: Synergizing artificial neural networks with SSP-RCP scenarios: Long-Term projection of residential electricity demand in China under climate-economic interactions
records.abstract: Amid escalating climate challenges, understanding the compound effects of economic and climatic drivers on residential electricity demand has become critical for sustainable energy planning. This study develops an integrated modeling framework combining econometric analysis with machine learning to forecast China's residential electricity consumption through 2100. Utilizing provincial-level panel data (2001–2019), we first employ fixed-effects regression to identify significant predictors. The results reveal that both economic variables (including per capita GDP [PGDP] and tertiary industry share [TIS]) and climatic variables (including Cooling/Heating Degree Days [CDD/HDD] and CO2 emissions [CO2]) exhibit statistically significant effects. These determinants are subsequently integrated into an artificial neural network (ANN) architecture enhanced with scenario analysis combining Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) and Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP). Our ANN-SSP-RCP hybrid integration reduces RMSE by 13.16 %–26.83 % versus traditional models by capturing nonlinear climate-economic dynamics. Key projections reveal: (1) Under deep decarbonization scenarios (2020–2060, compared to RCP4.5 and RCP8.5), early-stage decarbonization (RCP2.6) triggers a demand rebound of 1.51 %–2.39 % due to large-scale electrification; (2) By 2100, the impact of climate factors on China's residential electricity demand is 2.7 times greater than the impact of socioeconomic factors; (3) By 2100, residential electricity consumption in the high emissions scenario will be 100 billion kWh higher than in the low emissions scenario. The framework informs adaptive policies for grid resilience, regional energy-sharing, and rebound-effect mitigation, advancing China's dual-carbon targets amid climate-economy synergies across different development trajectories.

records.title: Algal bloom control through machine learning guided inverse design of pre-oxidation-coagulation
records.abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) threaten drinking water safety and ecosystem stability. Pre-oxidation–coagulation is an effective control method, but its operational optimization remains challenging due to nonlinear parameter interactions and limited systematic datasets. A machine learning–based inverse design framework was developed to optimize pre-oxidation–coagulation processes for algal removal. Literature data (n = 328) were supplemented with 471 newly conducted orthogonal experiments, yielding a balanced dataset (n = 799) covering nine oxidants, three coagulants, and pre-oxidation times from 5 to 60 min. A stacked ensemble model, employing CatBoost as the meta-learner over four base algorithms, was trained and interpreted using SHAP analysis. The model was coupled with sequential quadratic programming (SQP) for inverse parameter optimization, with target removal efficiency of 90 %. The ensemble model achieved an average test R2 = 0.783, with substantial gains for challenging oxidants such as K2FeO4 (+34.01 %). SHAP analysis ranked parameter importance as coagulant dose > oxidant dose > pre-oxidation time > oxidant type, revealing saturation of pre-oxidation effects within 5–20 min. Inverse design reduced experimental workload by over 98 % (384–6 validation runs) while maintaining ±8.34 % accuracy. Experimental validation (6 triplicate runs) confirmed both predictive reliability and process efficiency. Balanced datasets are critical for capturing oxidation-specific dynamics. The proposed framework offers a cost-effective, data-driven solution for rapid, precise HAB control, bridging laboratory studies with full-scale water treatment operations.

records.title: Integrating system dynamics and machine learning to establish the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus of aquavoltaics
records.abstract: Traditional aquaculture faces growing challenges from climate change, including rising water temperatures, reduced water availability, and declining yields. This study explores aquavoltaic systems—integrating aquaculture with solar panels—as a sustainable, climate-resilient solution. We used clam farming at the Mariculture Research Center Taihsi Station in Yunlin County, Taiwan, as a case study. Within the Water-Energy-Food-Climate-Land (WEFCL) nexus framework, we applied system dynamics (SD) modeling enhanced by a hybrid machine learning approach. By combining the genetic algorithm (GA) and the backpropagation neural network (BPNN), we improved the accuracy and reliability of SD models, simulating real-world conditions using in-situ monitoring datasets to promote sustainability, resource use efficiency, and policy coherence in aquaculture. Results show that 40 % solar panel shading reduced water temperatures by 2.5 °C, improved water use efficiency by 30 %, and generated renewable energy to offset emissions. Although clam yields declined by 27 %, solar power compensated for production losses, creating an economically viable system. Further optimization identified 45 % shading as ideal, preserving 70 % of yields while maximizing energy output. This study offers valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders, showcasing aquavoltaics as a scalable framework for balancing food production, renewable energy generation, and climate adaptation—advancing sustainable aquaculture in Taiwan and beyond.

records.title: Pre-optimization-based deep reinforcement learning for autonomous economic and exergy management of stochastic H2/CO ratio syngas switching downstream processes
records.abstract: Driven by global warming and escalating energy demand, sustainable syngas production continues to advance as an essential cleaner energy carrier. The switching of the syngas H2/CO ratio can supply tailored feedstock for synthesizing diverse downstream chemicals. However, unsteady state, stochastic behavior, and plant-model mismatch characteristics of the downstream process complicate existing control strategies and operational management. This study addresses the critical challenge of intelligent operational management in stochastic syngas switching downstream (SSSD) processes characterized by strong stochasticity and dynamic losses. To this end, a pre-optimization-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) control framework is proposed for autonomous economic and exergy (2E) management of SSSD process. First, a high-fidelity dynamic model of SSSD process is developed to simulate the stochastic behavior and dynamic losses of the system. Then, the optimization constraint algorithm is innovatively embedded into the DRL framework to obtain an optimized initial set of actions for each random reset. Finally, the agent is trained to interact with the dynamic model in pursuit of efficient exploration and reward, which produces an optimal control strategy. The proposed method reduces exergy destruction by 3.8 % and 2.1 % compared to proportional-integral-derivative (PID) and conventional DRL frameworks, while obtaining the minimum operating cost of $8542 and the most stable product control. The well-trained agent is also able to self-adapt to process uncertainties with higher exploration efficiency and stability, achieving intelligent and sustainable production for complex and dynamic processes.

records.title: Multi-step battery temperature prediction for electric vehicles: Vehicle identification-driven long short-term memory neural networks based on real-world charging pile data
records.abstract: Accurate prediction of battery temperature is critical for ensuring the safety of electric vehicles (EVs), which are pivotal for achieving cleaner transportation and reduced carbon emissions. Current research on battery temperature prediction relies primarily on laboratory or onboard battery management systems (BMS) data. However, these data sources have limitations in reflecting the complexity of real-world charging scenarios. In addition, the lack of vehicle identification information in charging pile data challenges accurate temperature prediction. To address this issue, this paper proposes a new approach that combines vehicle identification and grouping with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to predict battery temperature using real-world charging pile data. This study first proposes a multi-parameter disparity-based vehicle identification grouping (MPDVIG) strategy to group the charging data by vehicle identification. Then, the LSTM model is used to predict the temperature based on the overall and grouped data. By comparing the results of the two approaches, it is found that the accuracy of the method of identification followed by prediction is higher. For instance, the mean relative error for the highest temperature predictions decreased from 1.45 % to 1.06 %. This is the first time the LSTM model has been applied to the battery temperature prediction based on the real-world charging pile data, providing a reference for the subsequent safety warning.

records.title: Machine learning-optimized efficient CO2-to-CO conversion in a novel catalyst-free spark discharge plasma
records.abstract: Catalyst-free spark-discharge plasma offers a promising new route for CO2 utilization via the reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction, yet strong coupling among power, residence time, composition, and reactor geometry complicates deployment-relevant optimization. An improved coaxial quartz-tube spark-discharge reactor is considered, and a structured dataset of 500 operating points is compiled by varying discharge power, total flow rate, H2/CO2 molar ratio, and inner-tube diameter across engineering-relevant levels. To avoid inflated generalization caused by random splits on grid-like datasets, ten regressors are screened using leave-one-condition-out grouped cross-validation, and an artificial neural network (ANN; multilayer perceptron, MLP) surrogate is selected and tuned under the strict leave-one-diameter-out protocol with early stopping. Hyperparameter tuning improves grouped predictive accuracy to R2 = 0.909 for CO2 conversion and R2 = 0.970 for energy efficiency. Model credibility is further supported by bootstrap resampling, applicability-domain diagnostics, and external interpolation validation on 15 off-grid points (R2 = 0.907 for conversion and 0.959 for efficiency), with most observations captured within the 95 % prediction band. Operating-window maps identify a peak conversion of 89.76 % at 70 W, H2/CO2 = 3.0, 200 mL/min and an inner-tube diameter of 7 mm, and a peak energy efficiency of 19.12 % at 40 W, H2/CO2 = 1.0, 1000 mL/min and 7 mm, under bench-scale laboratory conditions. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) interpretation provides process-relevant attribution of nonlinear effects and clarifies interaction-driven regime dependence within the validated domain. The resulting workflow enables specification-driven, electricity-aware screening to finalize reactor configuration and operating windows for downstream syngas applications.

records.title: Attribution analysis of spatial differentiation in green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency based on geographical detector and random forest models: A case study of the Yangtze River Economic Belt
records.abstract: Green and low-carbon transition and development represents a global issue encompassing economic, social and environmental dimensions. To objectively assess the efficiency of this transition, this study establishes an evaluation index system from input-output perspectives of economy, resources and society, focusing on 108 prefecture-level cities along the Yangtze River Economic Belt. Through trend surface analysis and spatial autocorrelation methods, we investigate the spatio-temporal characteristics of green and low-carbon transition and development efficiency during 2011–2022. The geographical detector method integrated with random forest model is employed to identify driving factors. The main result are as follows: (1) Distinct spatial disparities in transition efficiency across the economic belt, with an overall upward trend despite suboptimal efficiency levels. Regional clusters demonstrate intensified agglomeration patterns, exhibiting a “high-east-west, low-central” spatial configuration. (2) Spatial positive correlations show increasing trends, with local spatial clusters predominantly manifesting as high-high or low-low agglomerations. (3) Dynamic variations in factor explanatory power across study years, with enhanced combined effects through factor interactions. Notably, the top three determinants, industrial development level, urban development level, and social consumption level exhibit nonlinear relationships with transition efficiency, while the nature of these relationships varies. This research provides empirical evidence for understanding regional transition mechanisms and offers decision-making support for formulating differentiated green development strategies.

records.title: A mechanistic machine learning framework to decode reverse osmosis membrane retention mechanism for neutral low-molecular-weight organics
records.abstract: Neutral low-molecular-weight (LMW) organics (e.g., urea, N-nitrosodimethylamine) with molecular weights <250 Da can permeate reverse osmosis (RO) membranes, compromising reclaimed water quality and posing health and industrial risks. However, the permeation characteristics of LMW organics and the mechanisms governing their retention are unclear. This study innovatively integrated data-driven machine learning (ML) with physicochemical mechanisms to decode RO retention characteristics and mechanisms of neutral LMW organics. A comprehensive database of 1254 retention data points for 190 organics was built, and six ML algorithms were evaluated. The XGBoost model, optimized via physicochemical mechanism-guided feature engineering (capturing steric, van der Waals, electrostatic, and hydrophobic interactions), achieved an adjusted R2 of 0.91 and MAE of 3.53%, outperforming traditional models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed steric and van der Waals effects as core retention mechanisms, with cross-mechanism synergies between steric and van der Waals interactions dominating retention. This framework mitigated data leakage (MAE reduced from 15.78% to 2.76% via compound-based splitting) and guided membrane design strategies: tuning pore size <0.4 nm for steric exclusion, enhancing polarizability for van der Waals adsorption, and optimizing pH-responsive charge layers. The study provided a transformative engineering roadmap for next-generation RO membranes, bridging data-driven predictions with mechanistic material design for sustainable water management.

records.title: Research on remote sensing ecological index prediction based on deep learning—Taking the application of long short-term memory neural network in Yili prefecture as an example
records.abstract: Ecological monitoring is often limited by the lag in post-event assessment, while predicting future ecological conditions is crucial for proactive environmental management. Therefore, we developed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network to predict the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) for the study area in 2025 and employed the Shapley Additive Interpretation (SHAP) method to explain the relative contributions of natural and anthropogenic factors. Studies show that drastic land-use change reduces prediction accuracy; therefore, we introduced a regional correction mechanism based on Bayesian conjugate priors to integrate land-use information into the deep learning prediction. This method was applied to the Ili region of Xinjiang, China, and performed well compared to measured data from 2020. Furthermore, its predicted regional average index for 2025 is consistent with the persistence indicated by the Hurst index. The study shows that ecological foundation and precipitation are the main positive drivers of future ecological quality, while high temperatures, soil drought, and intensive urbanization and grazing activities will reduce ecological quality. The results of the global bivariate Moran's index indicate a spatial correlation between land use change intensity and model residuals; areas with greater change are more likely to be adjacent to areas with larger prediction biases. Furthermore, we introduced a confidence parameter to measure the relative confidence between prior and predicted values and determined the optimal setting for balancing goodness of fit and robustness. Our research not only improves the model's predictive accuracy in areas of rapid land use transition, but also integrates spatial planning with ecological prediction. The findings support policymakers in anticipating multiple possible ecological outcomes when developing different regional planning pathways.

records.title: Climate dynamics and air quality interactions: Machine learning analysis of diurnal temperature range drivers in three major Bangladesh cities
records.abstract: Satellite-derived land surface temperature diurnal range (LST-DTR), computed as the difference between MODIS daytime and nighttime LST, acts as a meaningful proxy for surface radiative dynamics in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study employed three machine learning algorithms (Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Decision Tree) integrated with SHAP importance analysis to quantify the impacts of black carbon (BC), PM2.5, aerosol, and albedo on LST-DTR across three major Bangladesh cities: Dhaka, Chattogram, and Rajshahi. Satellite-derived MODIS and MERRA-2 data (2001-2023) were analyzed using 5-fold cross-validation, yielding moderate yet stable model performance (R2 = 0.35-0.43; RMSE = 2.04-2.51). SHAP analysis showed BC as the dominant predictor in all three cities (SHAP importance: 0.94-1.59), highlighting its key role in urban land surface thermal dynamics through radiative absorption and surface albedo modification. Albedo emerged as a key secondary factor (0.30–1.27), ranking highest in Rajshahi, where it nearly matched BC, while Aerosols ranked second in Dhaka and Chattogram (0.27–0.94), and PM2.5 had the weakest influence (0.08-0.35). The dominance of BC over PM2.5 in LST-DTR modulation suggests that current air quality policies, which primarily focus on particulate matter, may overlook the most critical driver of urban land-surface thermal variability. The study provides evidence for targeted actions: encouraging diesel particulate filters, updating kiln technology, urban greening with high-albedo vegetation in fast-growing zones, and cool roofing with reflective materials. These findings inform evidence-based environmental policies for sustainable urban development in rapidly expanding South Asian cities.

records.title: Longterm dynamics of plastisphere succession and polymer degradation mechanisms in marine environments: A 12-month in-situ study with machine learning applications
records.abstract: The escalating global crisis of marine plastic pollution underscores the urgent need to investigate longterm weathering mechanisms and associated ecological risks under environmental conditions. In this study, a 12-month in-situ exposure experiment was conducted in a subtropical marine environment to systematically elucidate the degradation dynamics of polypropylene (PP) and polylactic acid (PLA) and their interactions with microbial communities. Results demonstrate polymer-specific aging patterns and biofilm-enhanced risks, revealing that cyanobacteria (harmful algal bloom initiators) preferentially colonize persistent PP (12–15% abundance) over biodegradable PLA (0.22–0.26%). The persistence of PP in the environment enables stable cyanobacterial biofilms to act as longterm dispersal vectors for algal bloom initiation. In contrast, PLA surfaces were enriched with hydrolytic bacteria (e.g., Firmicutes), and this colonization was associated with enhanced mass loss and secondary microplastic formation. Furthermore, seasonal variations exerted limited control over dominant plastisphere taxa, with microbial communities on homogeneous plastics converging over time. Polymer type dominated plastisphere assembly, followed by exposure duration and physical form. Moreover, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN)-based machine learning (ML) model was developed to predict the weathering degree of plastics, achieving a highly reliable accuracy of 85.3 ± 0.8% by extracting image features of the weathered plastic surface, offering a novel paradigm for longterm ecological risk assessment. This work indicates that the short-term experiments are insufficient for predicting the fate of plastics and highlights the necessity of integrating multimodal data into extended observational frameworks and direct measures of microbial activity to evaluate ecological risks more accurately.

records.title: Corporate-level climate risk prediction: A comparative machine learning framework
records.abstract: Accurately predicting corporate climate risk is critical for climate-sensitive finance and policy. Using a panel of China's A-share listed firms (2004–2023), this study constructs a forward-looking, firm-specific climate-risk indicator via textual analysis of annual reports and integrates a comprehensive set of predictors that capture both internal firm characteristics and external climate-environmental exposure. Predictions are evaluated within a rigorous expanding-window out-of-sample framework that strictly prevents look-ahead bias. Systematic comparison of a broad spectrum of models—from classical econometric baselines to traditional machine learning and deep learning—reveals that advanced machine learning models collectively achieve an average out-of-sample R2 of 0.601, a 304.6% improvement over traditional baselines (average R2 = 0.149). Deep-learning architectures, especially Attention-LSTM (R2 = 0.815), LSTM, and CNN, deliver the highest predictive accuracy by capturing complex long-term temporal dependencies. Gradient-boosting trees (LightGBM, CatBoost) provide the best trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, whereas ensemble methods such as Stacking show robustness at higher computational cost. SHAP-based interpretability analysis of the best-performing models identifies debt investments the most influential predictor, with higher levels consistently associated with elevated climate-risk forecasts. Critically, externally measured climate variables—provincial physical-risk indices and city-level climate-policy uncertainty—rank among the top predictors, confirming that objective climate exposure and policy volatility are fundamental to the model's risk assessment. A counter-intuitive yet robust pattern is the positive contribution of green-patent counts, suggesting that firms facing strong transition pressure may be simultaneously active in green innovation. Interaction analysis further reveals that the marginal effect of debt investment is highly context-dependent, varying with internal firm attributes (age, asset structure, size) and external conditions (industry concentration, physical risk, institutional quality). This underscores that climate-risk formation is a non-linear outcome of coupled financial, organizational, and environmental factors. The study demonstrates the substantial predictive gain offered by machine learning, provides a granular mapping of algorithmic performance, and unveils the multidimensional, interactive statistical associations that drive climate-risk forecasts. These findings offer both methodological and empirical foundations for more resilient risk-management infrastructure and climate-informed decision-making.

records.title: Reinforcement learning control of pilot-scale solvent recovery for battery manufacturing: Surrogate-assisted optimization with techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment
records.abstract: As electric-vehicle battery manufacturing scales up, its environmental footprint grows, primarily driven by the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from using N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone in electrode fabrication. Establishing an efficient closed-loop recycling process for this solvent is therefore essential to advance a circular economy and align with emerging eco-design principles. To systematically minimize the GHG emissions of battery manufacturing, this study presents a surrogate-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the solvent recycling process, validated with data from a pilot-scale plant. The framework integrates a first-principles dynamic model developed in Aspen Plus Dynamics, a physics-constrained neural ordinary differential equation surrogate model, and an RL agent to jointly optimize reflux-ratio trajectories and batch termination under a stringent purity requirement of 99.99 wt%. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment modules translate control policies into quantitative production cost and GHG outcomes. As a result, the recycling process achieves GHG emissions of 0.222 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilogram of recovered solvent, compared to 8.06 kilograms for virgin production. Furthermore, the learned RL policies reduce production cost by up to 3.8% and decrease GHG emissions by up to 57%, relative to the worst-case fixed reflux ratio scenario. This pilot-validated framework provides a scalable pathway toward sustainable solvent-recovery practice in battery manufacturing, demonstrating that RL-based control can deliver both operational feasibility and environmental benefits.

records.title: Deciphering the multivariable interactions of MOFs in heavy metal adsorption via explainable machine learning for sustainable and resource-efficient adsorbent development
records.abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) in aquatic environments seriously threaten ecosystems and human health. Although metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have shown great potential for HMs removal, adsorption performance is governed by complex interactions between material characteristics and operating conditions. However, while existing studies largely emphasize performance prediction, systematic data-driven frameworks for decoding these interactions and guiding adsorbent design remain limited. This study constructed a comprehensive dataset comprising 4289 samples, incorporating MOF characteristics, experimental conditions, and adsorption data for Cr(VI), Pb(II), Cd(II), and As(V). Large-scale data mining was performed using explainable machine learning. Key findings include: the solution volume and shaker speed must be systematically investigated as critical parameters to enable a clear mechanistic discussion of the adsorption material and reliable performance comparison. The strong synergistic or antagonistic relationships between MOF components and experimental conditions were systematically explained as decisive for adsorption behaviors, highlighting the necessity of integrated parameter optimization for efficient adsorbent development and process design. The initial concentration of pollutants and reaction time showed significant interactive effects with other factors. In contrast, 95% of feature importance results consistently indicate that organic ligands exert a stronger influence on adsorption capacity, while coordination metals more readily affect removal rate. Finally, eight representative MOF compositions were identified for different environmental scenarios. This work establishes an explainable, data-driven decision-support framework that transforms adsorption data into actionable design knowledge, supporting resource-efficient material development and sustainable environmental remediation.

records.title: A process-informed framework for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for PPCPs by integrating machine learning and vadose-zone transport modeling
records.abstract: Conventional approaches for deriving groundwater-protective soil thresholds for pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) often simplify subsurface transport and neglect attenuation in the vadose zone, which can lead to overly conservative screening outcomes. To support more realistic and proportionate groundwater protection, this study developed a process-informed framework that integrates machine learning with HYDRUS-based vadose zone transport modeling. A global dataset covering 24 PPCPs and 584 soil and sediment samples was first used to predict the solid–liquid partition coefficient (Kd), and the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) model showed the best performance. The results indicated that molecular properties and soil organic carbon were the major controls on partitioning. Vadose zone attenuation factors (AF) were then quantified by coupling HYDRUS simulations with machine learning, and the best performing model achieved an R2 of 0.90. Depth, KOC, and precipitation were identified as the dominant controls on attenuation, accounting for 76% of the total contribution. By integrating Kd, AF, and groundwater dilution factor (DF), groundwater-protective soil thresholds were derived for trimethoprim, nalidixic acid, and niflumic acid, with HC5 values of 0.06, 0.80, and 41.12 mg kg−1, respectively. Compared with conventional EPA-style calculations, explicitly accounting for vadose-zone attenuation materially changed the threshold estimates. These findings demonstrate that explicit representation of vadose-zone processes improves the realism of soil screening and supports science-based site management and groundwater risk control for emerging contaminants.

records.title: Navigating the global expanse of offshore floating photovoltaics: Techno-ecological-economic boundaries decoded by artificial intelligence
records.abstract: Offshore floating photovoltaics (OFPV) offer a massive frontier for global clean energy without land competition, yet theoretical estimates ignore severe marine limitations and risks. This paper, for the first time, proposes a novel “virtual expert” framework to capture the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of marine environments for data-driven suitability assessment of global OFPV potential. Under current-stage assumptions, our analysis reveals that within Exclusive Economic Zones, stringent techno-environmental constraints curtail the initial 14,831,550 TWh/year (128.94 million km2) theoretical potential by 93.7%. This yields a realizable potential of 935,110 TWh/year across 9.04 million km2, underscoring the profound impact of technical and environmental thresholds on OFPV expansion. Regionally, Asia dominates in absolute potential, while Africa boasts the highest average suitability, with specific cyclone-exempt African nations achieving 100% “most suitable” coverage as promising early-stage deployment candidates. Constraint analysis identifies water depth as the primary physical barrier, eliminating vast high-radiance areas across Europe, the Americas, and Africa. Meanwhile, sea ice and marine protected areas impose absolute exclusions in high-latitude and ecological hotspots, whereas low-latitude deployments—notably in Asia and Oceania—demand robust tropical cyclone resilience. Furthermore, spatially resolved techno-economic assessments reveal that while unconstrained marine areas achieve an average levelized cost of energy of 9.16 US cents/kWh under standardized economic assumptions, some constrained zones nevertheless retain relatively favorable solar economics, suggesting that deep-water station-keeping and cyclone-resilient floating structures may become high-priority R&D directions for future OFPV innovation. Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that OFPV deployment is inherently a highly localized spatial optimization challenge, our framework providing a macro-siting tool to assist stakeholders in balancing clean energy expansion with marine conservation and environmental risk mitigation.

records.title: Interpretable machine learning reveals multi-scale controls on groundwater fluoride across the Shanxi rift system
records.abstract: Groundwater fluoride in the Shanxi Rift System displays marked spatial heterogeneity, with high-fluoride basins occurring adjacent to zones of totally low concentrations. This study investigates the factors responsible for this contrast by applying an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates supervised model comparison with posterior interpretation analyses. The modelling reveals a distinct scale dependence in fluoride controls. At the basin scale, fluoride enrichment is primarily influenced by hydrochemical conditions dominated by Ca2+ and HCO3−. At the cross-basin scale, however, the dominant control shifts to geological setting, particularly the distance to carbonate formations. Short distances correspond to higher Ca2+ and lower HCO3− conditions, resulting in hydrochemical “non-responsive intervals” in which fluoride concentrations remain low and insensitive to further changes in Ca2+ and HCO3−. This mechanism accounts for the anomalously low fluoride levels observed in the Changzhi Basin. Overall, the results demonstrate that fluoride distribution in the Shanxi Rift System is shaped by the combined effects of local hydrochemical equilibria and regional geological structure, and highlight the importance of explicitly considering spatial scale when interpreting the processes governing geogenic fluoride contamination.

records.title: Auto-optimized interpretable machine learning for terminal water quality prediction of the ultrapure water production system in the semiconductor industry: demonstration in a full-scale system
records.abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, maintaining ultrapure water (UPW) quality at the terminal is critical for product safety. However, early prediction and warning of water quality deterioration remain challenging due to complex process interactions and limited monitoring responsiveness. This study developed interpretable machine learning models for 1-h-ahead prediction of terminal total organic carbon (TOC) and resistivity in a full-scale UPW system (48 m3/d). Six modeling approaches were evaluated, and XGBoost and Random Forest (RF) were selected as the optimal models for TOC and resistivity prediction, respectively. After hyperparameter optimization, the Optuna-XGBoost model achieved an R2 of 0.9664 for TOC prediction, while the RS-RF model achieved an R2 of 0.9670 for resistivity prediction. Model interpretation using SHAP and partial dependence analysis identified return water resistivity as a key influencing factor for both targets, suggesting that return water may act as a potential risk source. Strong nonlinear interaction effects were observed, particularly between first- and second-stage RO rejection rates for TOC prediction, and between return water resistivity and first-stage RO rejection for resistivity prediction. In addition, models were developed for RO membrane rejection rates. First-stage rejection was mainly governed by historical behavior, whereas second-stage rejection depended on influent conductivity and operational conditions. The proposed framework enables reliable 1-h-ahead prediction and early warning of water quality deterioration, supporting proactive operational strategies such as return water management and RO/VUV/mixed bed optimization. Overall, this work demonstrates the value of interpretable auto machine learning for early warning and decision support in semiconductor UPW systems.

records.title: An integrated machine learning and MATLAB/Simulink framework for enhanced photovoltaic power forecasting and grid integration
records.abstract: The rapid integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into modern power grids requires energy forecasting approaches that are both statistically accurate and physically consistent. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines machine–learning–based prediction with physics-based validation in MATLAB/Simulink. The key contribution is a two-layer validation workflow in which data-driven ensemble forecasts are evaluated against a grid-connected PV simulation model to assess their physical feasibility under realistic operating conditions. The proposed framework employs a stacking ensemble that integrates complementary tree-based and neural-network-based learners and is evaluated across multiple datasets, including reanalysis-based meteorological data and field-measured PV outputs. Results show that the stacking ensemble achieves an RMSE of 0.022, MAE of 0.011, and R2 of 0.996 on the reanalysis-based dataset (MERRA-2). On real-world (Northern Hemisphere) PV data, the model achieves an RMSE of 4.7211 W, MAE of 3.5061 W, and R2 of 0.5612, while independent meteorological data (NSRDB) yield an RMSE of 0.0554 W, MAE of 0.0297 W, and R2 of 0.9815, demonstrating competitive performance across different operating conditions. Statistical comparisons indicate that the ensemble achieves significant improvements in MAE relative to benchmark models in selected datasets while remaining competitive on RMSE. To enhance interpretability, LIME-based analysis is used to quantify the influence of meteorological features, and ablation studies are conducted to assess the contribution and robustness of the ensemble architecture. Physics-based validation using a 10-kW grid-connected Simulink model demonstrates that the predicted power trajectories are consistent with converter dynamics and operational constraints, with an average deviation of approximately 3% and an RMSE of 0.182 kW between the machine-learning predictions and simulation outputs. Additional validation using reanalysis data from Tamil Nadu indicates promising generalization, although evaluation remains limited to specific sites and conditions. Long-term forecasting that incorporates degradation effects is also explored to extend the framework for planning applications. Overall, the proposed approach provides a structured pathway for integrating data-driven forecasting with engineering validation, enabling more reliable renewable energy integration, improved energy management, and resource-efficient grid operations that support the transition toward cleaner electricity production.

records.title: Interpretable machine learning insights into the impact of environmental regulation on low-carbon transition: Evidence from the Yangtze River Economic Belt
records.abstract: Environmental regulation (ER) has become an important instrument for achieving environmental goals and advancing the low-carbon transition (LCT). However, existing studies still suffer from several limitations, including incomplete indicator systems, difficulties in capturing the nonlinear relationship and multifactor interaction effects between ER and LCT, and a lack of empirical analyses at the watershed scale. Consequently, the mechanism through which ER affects LCT warrants further in-depth exploration. To address these gaps, this study employs panel data from 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt from 2010 to 2023 to reveal the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics of ER and LCT and applies the XGBoost-SHAP model to identify the impact of ER on LCT. The results show that: (1) the spatial patterns of both ER and LCT present high values in the east and low values in the west, with high-value areas gradually agglomerating toward core regions, such as the Yangtze River Delta; (2) ER contributes 20.87% to LCT and exhibits a significant threshold effect, with its positive impact increasing markedly when ER exceeds 0.338; (3) synergistic effects between ER and factors such as urban transportation and financial development significantly enhance LCT. This study constructed a multidimensional evaluation system for ER and LCT and, for the first time, revealed the nonlinear threshold mechanism and multifactor synergy rules of ER affecting LCT at the watershed scale of the Yangtze River Economic Belt. This provides new empirical evidence for understanding their interaction mechanism and offers implications for optimizing the LCT pathways in this region.

records.title: Attributing streamflow extremes under compound scenarios via hybrid of explainable AI and hydrological modeling: Implications for sustainable watershed management
records.abstract: Accurate projection and attribution of streamflow extremes under compound climate and climate and land-use scenarios are critical for sustainable watershed management, yet conventional assessments predominantly evaluate isolated factors and overlook dynamic anthropogenic regulations. This study develops an integrated scenario-based hybrid attribution analysis of streamflow extremes (abbreviated as SHASE) framework for (i) tackling non-linear boundary inflows and reservoir dispatches via a mass-conserving explainable AI (GBR-SHAP) topology; (ii) capturing the regulatory streamflow reshaping by extracting extreme quantiles (Q10, Q50, Q90) from empirical Flow Duration Curves (FDCs); (iii) quantifying the individual and interactive effects of climate and land-use on different subbasins using analysis of variance (ANOVA). The SHASE framework is applied to the “Ji"-shaped region of the Yellow River Basin. Key findings indicate: (1) GBR-SHAP feature sensitivities reveal empirical response patterns that align with known catchment moisture memory (dominated by 12-month rolling precipitation); (2) FDC analyses reveal an asymmetric flow-reshaping effect along the regulated channel, where reservoir operations truncate wet-season high flows (Q10) while supplementing dry-season low flows (Q90); (3) while climate change acts as the dominant macro-scale driver across more than 75% of the watershed (contributing over 76% of streamflow variance on average), urban surface hardening triggered high flow in 12.5% of the subbasins, while the interaction between climate and land use dominated the low-flow deficits in 20.0% of the subbasins during dry-season. The findings suggest that achieving sustainable watershed management requires a shift from isolated climate assessment to integrated climate-land-water coordination that addresses the local extreme-flow drivers in strictly regulated watersheds.

records.title: An efficient conditional diffusion model for meteorological data super-resolution based on stochastic differential equations over Eastern China
records.abstract: Global weather forecasts provide essential support for socioeconomic activities, but their applications remain constrained by coarse spatial resolution and systematic, regime-dependent biases, particularly over meteorologically heterogeneous regions. This study develops a conditional diffusion model based on stochastic differential equations, which integrates intensity-boundary structural learning with adaptive refinement via dynamic convolution and channel attention to produce high-resolution meteorological fields across multiple forecast products. Evaluations over Eastern China against ERA5-Land show that the super-resolution forecasts achieve strong agreement with the reference, with temperature and wind fields at a 12 h lead time reaching R2 values of up to about 0.90 and 0.87, respectively, and precipitation event skill reaching stable equitable error in probability space (SEEPS) values as low as approximately 0.05, consistently outperforming interpolation-based and deterministic learning methods. Compared with representative baseline models, the proposed framework demonstrates more robust performance across variables and forecast settings, with improved preservation of coherent spatial distributions, localized gradients, and extreme-value features. Using the super-resolution weather forecasts, we further demonstrate an application to gridded daily maximum 8 h ozone prediction. Compared with ozone predictions driven by the low-resolution meteorological fields, the use of super-resolved meteorological fields yields systematic improvements in predictive performance, with R2 increased by 4.6–5.8%. For the evaluated forecast products and meteorological variables over Eastern China, these results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for regional-scale forecast refinement and downstream air-quality prediction.

records.title: Target dependent cleaner production screening of recycling pathways for end of life electric vehicle lithium ion batteries using an interpretable machine learning framework
records.abstract: Which recycling route is preferred when the decision target, proxy boundary, functional-unit scaling, and model-use domain change? This study developed an auditable, time-indexed scenario-screening framework for end-of-life electric-vehicle lithium-ion batteries. The deterministic grid contains 1008 designed combinations representing structured scenarios rather than plant observations. A prespecified 168-row subset of 84 paired physical configurations supported machine-learning (ML) evaluation. Six targets include process energy; operational energy-related CO2 burden limited to grid electricity and direct diesel/natural-gas combustion; a spend-proxy-credit-adjusted screening balance; and three mapped economic indicators. The adjusted balance subtracts spend-normalized recovered-material proxies from the narrower operational burden and serves as a screening indicator within this partial boundary. Pack values provide a cross-model mass-intensity sensitivity; a full pack-level life-cycle inventory lies outside the analysis. All 12 target-basis tasks used five-fold physical-configuration-grouped evaluation. For each task, grouped and route-held-out learners were selected separately by minimum mean root-mean-square error (RMSE). For adjusted balance, grouped RMSE and coefficient of determination (R2) values were 0.0816/0.99990 (cell) and 0.4561/0.99481 (pack); the corresponding lowest task-level route-held-out RMSEs were 7.0693 and 6.1501. Dependence-aware uncertainty analyses of the carbon-dioxide-equivalent (CO2e) indicators selected hydrometallurgical recycling for operational burden and direct recycling for fully credited adjusted balance under the specified screening assumptions. Removing the active-cathode spend proxy shifted the lower adjusted balance to hydrometallurgical recycling. Route preference changed across targets. The framework supports conditional screening and evidence prioritization within represented route families. Full life-cycle climate assessment requires complete inventories and verified substitution evidence. Application to a new route requires foreground data and revalidation.

records.title: Decoupling hydrological and economic drivers of global rainwater harvesting performance using explainable artificial intelligence
records.abstract: Decentralized rainwater harvesting (RWH) is critical for urban water resilience, yet current research remains fragmented, relying on site-specific case studies that limit the identification of transferable physical and economic patterns across heterogeneous urban contexts. Here, we present a unified, data-driven framework that harmonizes 3879 RWH cases across 179 cities into a globally consistent dataset. We developed predictive models for key economic and water-saving performance indicators, including benefit-cost ratio (BCR), Net Present Value (NPV), payback period (PBP), and water-saving efficiency (WSE). The predictive framework employs a Bayesian-optimized Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) integrated with interpretability algorithms. Model robustness was evaluated using random-split, study-isolated, and geographic extrapolation tests. Across the four targets, R2 values ranged from 0.928 to 0.960 under random split and 0.656–0.868 under study-isolated validation. Geographic transferability was scale-dependent: city-level extrapolation retained R2 values of 0.740–0.892, whereas country-level extrapolation declined markedly to 0.323–0.511. SHAP-based interpretation revealed nonlinear feature interactions and indicator-specific contribution patterns, with catchment fraction identified as a key predictor reflecting the influence of system scale matching between contributing area and harvesting capacity within the compiled dataset. These results support the framework as an interpretable screening and scenario-comparison tool within the climatic, socioeconomic, and system domains represented by the compiled dataset, while indicating that applications to substantially different national contexts require local calibration and additional validation.

records.title: Descriptor-resolved machine learning reveals response patterns and molecular interaction differences in MOF-based removal of hazardous aromatic pollutants
records.abstract: High adsorption capacities reported for MOF-based systems may reflect specific combinations of material, pollutant, and operating descriptors rather than transferable material performance. Here, a descriptor-resolved framework integrating literature-derived adsorption records, interpretable machine learning, sensitivity analysis, and representative molecular calculations was developed to distinguish response structure within the represented data domain from cross-publication transferability. The XGBoost model using CMAES-derived hyperparameters achieved a pooled out-of-fold R2 of 0.953 under record-level validation, whereas performance decreased markedly to R2 = −0.221 under publication-grouped validation. Despite this decline, the global descriptor-contribution hierarchy remained highly stable across the two validation schemes (ρ = 0.985), with initial concentration and adsorbent dosage ranking highest. Because both variables are mathematically linked to adsorption capacity, targeted feature-removal analysis was further performed. After simultaneously excluding them, the model retained an out-of-fold R2 of 0.854, while adsorption time, particle size, specific surface area, pore size, and pKa emerged as the highest-contributing descriptors. Representative paired response maps from the reduced model further revealed localized and non-monotonic associations among operating, material, and pollutant descriptors within the sampled domain. Molecular calculations showed that linker functionalization did not uniformly strengthen pollutant binding; instead, interaction stability depended on pollutant identity, aromatic contact, polar interaction, molecular orientation, and local linker chemistry. Overall, the framework distinguishes comparatively stable descriptor-response patterns from the more limited transferability of absolute adsorption-capacity predictions, providing a more rigorous basis for interpreting heterogeneous MOF adsorption evidence and prioritizing response patterns for independent experimental validation.

records.title: Physics-informed graph modeling for traffic shockwave analysis through optimized change-point detection
records.abstract: Shockwaves represent one of the most consequential and pervasive disturbances in highway operations, yet existing shockwave identification methods struggle to capture the underlying causal mechanisms. This paper introduces a novel framework that fundamentally reconceptualizes driver dynamics through graph theory, redefining shockwave formation and dissipation as chains of causally linked braking and acceleration behaviors. The methodology employs an optimized Change Point Detection (CPD) algorithm to segment individual vehicle trajectories and identify significant acceleration and deceleration events at the microscopic level. A graph-based clustering technique then connects these events across multiple vehicles, explicitly capturing the inherent causation of shockwave propagation by tracing how one vehicle’s deceleration triggers a cascade of braking responses in following vehicles, propagating upstream against the direction of traffic flow. This approach transforms shockwave identification from a statistical classification problem into a network propagation perspective, ensuring the detection of physically reasonable propagation waves that reflect actual driver-to-driver interactions. Comprehensive performance evaluation against baseline methods demonstrates the superiority of the framework in characterizing key shockwave properties, including propagation speed, spatial extent, duration, and oscillation intensity. Through sensitivity analysis and ablation study, this approach has been proved a robust foundation for traffic flow analysis, effectively bridging microscopic driver behaviors with macroscopic flow phenomena through the lens of graph modeling methodology.

records.title: Advancing molecular property prediction for environmental fate using graph neural networks: A comparative analysis
records.abstract: In cheminformatics, predicting molecular properties is crucial for enhancing material research, toxicity assessment and drug discovery. This research investigates the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for predicting molecular properties by examining three different architectures: Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN), Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) and Graphormer. We show that GNNs that include structural and geometric information perform noticeably better than conventional descriptor-based machine learning models using benchmark datasets like as QM9, ZINC, and OGB-MolHIV. This study further plays a pivotal role in understanding the environmental fate and transport of chemical compounds by find partition coefficients like Octanol-Water Partition Coefficient (Kow), Air-Water Partition Coefficient (Kaw) and Soil-Water Partition Coefficient (K_d). Graphormer achieves the best performance on log Kow (MAE = 0.18) and MolHIV classification (ROC-AUC = 0.807). EGNN with its E(n)-equivariant updates and 3D coordinate integration achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) on geometry-sensitive properties like log Kaw (0.25) and log K_d (0.22). The significance of architectural alignment with molecular property traits is underscored by these findings.

records.title: SigmaCCS2: Collision cross section prediction using molecular topological and geometric information with graph neural network
records.abstract: Collision cross section (CCS) values are crucial for compound characterization in ion mobility spectrometry (IMS), yet their experimental determination is often resource-intensive. To overcome this, we introduce SigmaCCS2, a graph neural network (GNN)-based method that predicts CCS values by integrating both molecular topological and geometric information. By representing molecules as dual graphs, where molecular graphs encode topological structures and line graphs encode molecular geometries, SigmaCCS2 captures comprehensive structural features for accurate predictions. This approach achieves highly competitive and robust predictive performance, generally superior or comparable to state-of-the-art methods on external test sets. SigmaCCS2 demonstrates robust versatility across different instruments and molecular superclasses. Furthermore, a user-friendly web server is provided, enhancing accessibility for researchers. This advancement in CCS prediction enhances compound identification in various fields, including metabolomics, lipidomics, and drug discovery, by improving CCS coverage in databases.

records.title: Explainable machine learning enables robust evaluation of extracted ion chromatograms in LC–MS metabolomics
records.abstract: Reliable evaluation of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) remains a persistent challenge in LC–MS metabolomics, as inaccuracies in peak identification can profoundly impact subsequent data analysis and interpretation. While recent deep learning approaches show promise, their computational burden, limited generalizability, and lack of interpretability hinder broad adoption in routine analytical workflows. To address these limitations, we introduce EXACT-EIC (EXplainable Assessment of Chromatogram qualiTy for EICs), a lightweight, explainable machine learning framework. EXACT-EIC employs a thoughtfully designed 34 handcrafted features to perform two critical tasks: effective binary classification of EICs (peak vs. noise) and quantitative quality scoring. Benchmarking on curated in-house and public testing set demonstrated that EXACT-EIC achieved 95.2 % accuracy and 98.1 % recall for classification. For quantitative assessment, it attained a mean absolute error of 0.70 on a 1–10 expert-assigned quality scale. These results consistently outperformed state-of-the-art deep learning methods including PeakOnly and QuanFormer. Furthermore, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified the contribution of key chromatographic features (e.g., apex-boundary ratio, distribution entropy) to model predictions, offering transparent mechanistic insights absent in "black-box" architectures. By combining robustness, interpretability, and computational efficiency, EXACT-EIC facilitates reliable EIC evaluation across diverse platforms and experimental conditions. It provides a practical, deployable solution for automated quality control and confident metabolite annotation, addressing a critical need in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics workflows.

records.title: Multimodal class-aware molecule language model for drug response prediction
records.abstract: Drug response prediction driven by artificial intelligence (AI) offers an efficient solution for accelerating the development of precision medicine and personalized treatment. However, existing AI methods are typically limited by high noise levels, heterogeneity, and limited modal data. These limitations decrease model performance and hinder the identification of critical biomarkers. Therefore, we propose a Multimodal Class-Aware Molecular Language (MCML) model for accurate drug response prediction. Specifically, MCML systematically integrates multimodal features of drugs and cell lines and establishes a crossmodal modeling mechanism to achieve deep fusion of multimodal information. Meanwhile, the model dynamically adjusts the contribution weights based on the class features and importance of the samples, effectively alleviating the noise interference inherent in multimodal data. Furthermore, MCML employs self-supervised learning for pre-training to capture potential molecular interaction patterns, enhancing its ability to adapt to data heterogeneity. Experiments performed on cross-scale multiomics datasets and single-cell transcriptomic data indicate that MCML significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in RMSE and MAE scores. These case studies further demonstrate that the MCML model can effectively identify tumor microenvironment characteristics associated with drug resistance, demonstrating its ability to discover relevant biomarkers. Additionally, we performed an interpretability analysis of the model to investigate the impact of key features on the prediction results. This research establishes a new methodological paradigm for multimodal tumor data-driven drug response predictions and offers reliable computational tools for personalized cancer treatment decision making.

records.title: Comparative evaluation of lightweight convolutional neural network and vision transformer models for multi-class brain tumor classification using merged large MRI datasets
records.abstract: The accurate classification of brain tumors from MRI scans is important for the timely diagnosis and treatment planning process; however, previous state-of-the-art automatic image classification methods frequently struggle to balance performance with computational cost for clinical applications. In this study, we evaluated twenty lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) models and eighteen Vision Transformers (ViT) models for multi-class brain tumor classification using a merged dataset of 17,933 MRI images from 4 categories (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumors, and healthy brains). The study demonstrated that both groups of architectures can achieve state-of-the-art performance with EfficientNet-b0 (98.36 % accuracy, 4.01 M params) and Tiny-ViT-5M (98.41 % accuracy, 5.07 M params), ranking as the top-performing models for each category. The systematic comparison determined that the proposed lighter models have equivalent or greater performance than established lightweight frameworks, while offering computational advantages, such as MobileViT-xxSmall, which achieved outstanding performance (98.16 % accuracy) with fewer than 1 M parameters. Through benchmarking against fourteen other prior existing frameworks for brain tumor classification, we demonstrated that the top-performing lightweight models of this study maintain stable performances across all evaluation metrics (including precision, recall, and F1 score) and aim to mitigate key weaknesses of prior work, including dataset diversity and model complexity. The findings show very competitive performance across brain tumor classification, highlighting the promise of lightweight architectures to generate accurate and efficient diagnostic support for potential clinical deployment, particularly in low-resource healthcare environments where such efficiencies are vital. Moreover, this work provides useful knowledge that may assist in developing deployable artificial intelligence solutions in neuro-oncology settings.

records.title: Explainable AI for secure and accurate prediction of bacteriophage virion proteins using NLP descriptors and transformer-guided ideal proximity matrix reconstruction
records.abstract: The biological functions of bacteria are significantly impacted by bacteriophage virion proteins (BVPs), which are bacterial viruses. BVPs play a major role in phage therapy and genetic engineering. Secure and accurate identification of these proteins is essential for understanding phage-host interactions and for bioinformatics and medical applications. However, ensuring privacy and robustness in computational models is challenging, especially when handling complex biological data. Previous works relied on wet-lab experiments, had limited scalability, incomplete feature coverage, and low generalization ability. In this study, we introduce a privacy-preserving and adversarial-robust deep learning framework.
